_meta.description: Static deterministic pathway data for food claim concept guidance. Not regulatory advice.

pathways.name: Probiotic route
pathways.description: Contains specific live bacterial strains at substantiated CFU levels.
requirements: Identified strain(s) with Lactobacillus or Bifidobacterium genus/species/strain
Minimum viable CFU count at end-of-shelf-life (not just at manufacture)
Evidence linking specific strain to claimed function
Survival through product matrix to end of shelf life

pathways.name: Prebiotic fibre route
pathways.description: Contains dietary fibre that selectively feeds beneficial gut bacteria.
requirements: Quantified fibre content per serve
Identified fibre type (inulin, FOS, GOS, PHGG, resistant starch, pectin)
Meets FSANZ high-fibre threshold if making high-fibre claim
Evidence for fermentability and prebiotic effect of selected fibre

pathways.name: Fermented culture route
pathways.description: Contains live fermented dairy or food cultures contributing to digestive wellbeing.
requirements: Confirmed live cultures present at point of consumption
Culture identity declared
Claim limited to general digestive wellbeing — not specific strain health claims

safer_wording: Contains fibre to support digestive wellbeing
information_needed: CFU count at end of shelf life (not manufacture date)
Fibre type and quantity per serve
Shelf life and storage conditions (live cultures must survive)
Any therapeutic or disease claims intended
next_questions: Does the product contain live probiotic cultures — if so, what specific strains?
What is the CFU count at end of shelf life?
Does the product contain added prebiotic fibre — if so, what type and how much per serve?
Is the product dairy-based, plant-based, or other?
What is the intended claim — general digestive wellbeing or a specific function?

pathways.name: Vitamin C route
pathways.description: Vitamin C contributes to the normal function of the immune system.
requirements: Minimum 15% RDI vitamin C per serve for 'source of' claim
Minimum 30% RDI per serve for 'good source of' claim
Declared on nutrition information panel
FSANZ Standard 1.2.7 / 1.3.2 compliance

pathways.name: Zinc route
pathways.description: Zinc contributes to the normal function of the immune system.
requirements: Minimum 25% RDI zinc per serve
Form of zinc with acceptable bioavailability
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Vitamin D route
pathways.description: Vitamin D contributes to the normal function of the immune system.
requirements: Minimum 25% RDI vitamin D per serve
Stability data for vitamin D in product matrix
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Probiotic route
pathways.description: Specific probiotic strains with evidence for immune modulation.
requirements: Strain-specific evidence for immune function
CFU count at end of shelf life
Claim linked to specific strain, not general probiotics

safer_wording: Contains vitamin C to support normal immune function
A source of zinc, which supports normal immune function
Contains vitamin D to support immune health
information_needed: Vitamin C, zinc, vitamin D content per serve
% RDI of key nutrients per serve
Any therapeutic intent or disease prevention claims planned
next_questions: What micronutrients does the product contain that are relevant to immune function?
What is the % RDI of vitamin C, zinc, or vitamin D per serve?
Is the intended claim nutrient-based or structure/function based?
Are any specific pathogens or diseases referenced in the intended claim?

pathways.name: B vitamins route
pathways.description: B vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12, folate) contribute to normal energy-yielding metabolism.
requirements: Minimum 25% RDI per serve for at least one B vitamin
Declared on nutrition information panel
Claim tied to metabolic function, not subjective energy sensation

pathways.name: Iron route
pathways.description: Iron contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism and reduction of tiredness.
requirements: Minimum 25% RDI iron per serve
Form of iron with good bioavailability
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Low GI / sustained energy route
pathways.description: Carbohydrates with low glycaemic index providing sustained energy release.
requirements: GI testing of product by accredited laboratory
Low GI certification or supporting GI data
Claim framed around slow energy release, not boosting energy

safer_wording: Contains B vitamins to support normal energy metabolism
A source of iron, which contributes to normal energy metabolism
information_needed: B vitamin content and % RDI per serve
Iron content and % RDI per serve
Carbohydrate source and GI data if relevant
next_questions: Does the product contain B vitamins — which ones and at what % RDI per serve?
Does the product contain iron — in what form and at what level?
Is the energy claim based on nutrient content or carbohydrate GI?
Is the target audience a general healthy population or a specific group?

pathways.name: Protein route
pathways.description: Protein contributes to the maintenance and growth of muscle mass.
requirements: Minimum 10g protein per serve for meaningful claim
Complete amino acid profile or declared essential amino acids
High-quality protein source (PDCAAS or DIAAS score)
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Magnesium route
pathways.description: Magnesium contributes to normal muscle function.
requirements: Minimum 25% RDI magnesium per serve
Form with good bioavailability (citrate, glycinate, malate)
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Electrolyte route
pathways.description: Electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium) support normal muscle function during exercise.
requirements: Declared sodium, potassium, magnesium levels
Context of use framed around active/sporting consumers
Not framed as treatment for cramping or injury

safer_wording: Contains magnesium which contributes to normal muscle function
A source of protein for muscle maintenance and growth
information_needed: Protein content and source per serve
Target consumer — general population or active/sporting?
next_questions: How many grams of protein per serve?
What is the protein source (whey, pea, soy, collagen)?
Does the product contain added electrolytes or magnesium?
Is the target consumer an active or sporting individual?
Is there any therapeutic intent (injury recovery, disease treatment)?

pathways.name: Electrolyte replenishment route
pathways.description: Product contains electrolytes lost through sweat to support hydration during exercise.
requirements: Declared electrolyte levels (sodium, potassium, magnesium)
Claim framed in context of exercise or physical activity
Osmolality data for isotonic claims

pathways.name: Water content route
pathways.description: High water content food contributing to daily fluid intake.
requirements: No specific nutrient required
Claim framed generally — contributes to fluid intake
Not making disease/medical claims

information_needed: Sodium, potassium, magnesium content per serve
next_questions: What electrolytes does the product contain and at what levels?
Is the product intended for use during or after exercise?
Is an isotonic claim intended?
What is the sodium content per 100mL?

pathways.name: Calcium route

requirements: Minimum 25% RDI calcium per serve (250mg)
Bioavailable form of calcium
Declared on nutrition information panel
Vitamin D co-presence improves claim credibility

pathways.name: Vitamin D route
pathways.description: Vitamin D is needed for normal absorption and utilisation of calcium and normal maintenance of bones.
requirements: Minimum 25% RDI vitamin D per serve
Stability data for product matrix
Often used in conjunction with calcium claim

safer_wording: Calcium is needed for the maintenance of normal bones
Contains calcium and vitamin D to support bone health
information_needed: Calcium content and % RDI per serve
Product matrix and bioavailability of calcium form
next_questions: How much calcium is in the product per serve?
Is vitamin D included to support calcium absorption?
What form of calcium is used?
Is the product dairy or plant-based?

requirements: Minimum 25% RDI vitamin E per serve
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Vitamin C route
pathways.description: Vitamin C contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress.
requirements: Minimum 15% RDI vitamin C per serve
Declared on nutrition information panel

pathways.name: Selenium route
pathways.description: Selenium contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress.

Bioavailable form of selenium

pathways.name: Polyphenol / botanical route
pathways.description: Products high in polyphenols with general antioxidant characterisation.
requirements: ORAC or FRAP antioxidant capacity data
Identified polyphenol source
Claim limited to general antioxidant characterisation, not disease prevention

ORAC or antioxidant capacity data if available
next_questions: What is the primary antioxidant source in the product?

pathways.name: Plant sterol route
pathways.description: Plant sterols reduce blood cholesterol — well-established FSANZ-approved pathway.
requirements: Minimum 0.8g plant sterols per serve
Product complies with FSANZ Standard 1.2.7 Schedule 4
Mandated advisory statement for specific populations
Claim wording must follow permitted format

pathways.name: Beta-glucan route
pathways.description: Oat beta-glucan reduces blood cholesterol — FSANZ-approved claim.
requirements: Minimum 3g beta-glucan per day from oat sources
Product context is oat-based food
Claim wording follows FSANZ permitted format

pathways.name: Omega-3 route
pathways.description: DHA and EPA contribute to normal heart function.
requirements: Minimum 250mg combined EPA+DHA per serve for general heart health reference
Higher amounts for lipid-related claims
Source (fish oil, algal oil) declared

safer_wording: Contains plant sterols which have been shown to reduce blood cholesterol
Oat beta-glucan helps reduce cholesterol when consumed as part of a balanced diet
Contains omega-3 DHA which contributes to the maintenance of normal blood triglyceride levels
information_needed: Plant sterol level per serve (if applicable)
EPA and DHA content per serve (if applicable)
next_questions: Does the product contain plant sterols — at what level per serve?
Is the product oat-based and does it contain beta-glucan?
What is the EPA and DHA content per serve?
Is any blood pressure or cardiovascular disease claim intended?
Has the product been reviewed by a food regulatory expert for heart health claims?

pathways.name: No sugar claim route
pathways.description: Product contains no sugars as defined by FSANZ.
requirements: Sugars content ≤0.5g per 100g/100mL (FSANZ Standard 1.2.7)
No added sugars of any kind
Nutrition information panel must display sugars row

pathways.name: Reduced sugar claim route
pathways.description: Product contains at least 25% less sugar than reference product.
requirements: At least 25% reduction compared to reference product
Reference product clearly identified
Absolute reduction of at least 5g per 100g or 2.5g per 100mL
Claim format: 'X% less sugar than [reference]'

pathways.name: No added sugar claim route
pathways.description: No sugars or ingredients containing sugars added during manufacture.
requirements: No added sugars of any type (including fruit juice concentrates, honey, syrups)
Natural sugars may still be present (e.g. from fruit, dairy)
Claim: 'No added sugar' per FSANZ Standard 1.2.7

information_needed: Any added sugars including fruit juice concentrates, honey, syrups
next_questions: What is the total sugars content per 100g or 100mL?
Are any added sugars present — including honey, syrups, or fruit juice concentrates?
Does the product use non-nutritive sweeteners — if so, which ones?
Is any blood glucose or diabetes claim intended?

pathways.name: High protein claim route

requirements: ≥10g protein per serve (solid food) or ≥5g per serve (beverage)
Minimum 20% energy from protein per serve

FSANZ Standard 1.2.7 Schedule 4 compliance

pathways.name: Source of protein claim route
pathways.description: Product is a source of protein — lower threshold than 'high protein'.

Minimum 10% energy from protein per serve
Declared on nutrition information panel

avoid_wording: Replaces meals for medical weight management
information_needed: Protein content per serve in grams
next_questions: How many grams of protein are in the product per serve?
What percentage of energy per serve comes from protein?
